body.p: Natively, P-cores and E-cores have different instruction set by architecture. The direction is to support Symmetric Instruction Set Architecture across both core types, however, E-cores do not support full set of P-core instructions (such as AVX3), at the same time, some E-core instructions are not supported in P-cores.
Most of the MSRs are converged, however, a few model specific registers have new definitions from previous processor generations. For example:

ul.li: SMM delay and SMM blocked MSRs, offset 0x4E2 and 0x4E3 are one of those impacted MSRs. The converged solution for the SMM delay and blocked are define them as counters instead of bit vectors.

Turbo Ratio Limit MSRs. Because the E-cores generally have much lower max non-turbo ration than P-cores, therefore, the Turbo Ratio Limits MSRs need to be done separately:
For P-cores, they are MSR offset 0x1AD and 0x1AE as a pair
E-cores are MSR offset 0x650 and 0x651 as a pair

body.p: The paired registers define ratio limits and map the active core ranges for each frequency point.
